title: Grateful Dead Live at Santa Fe Downs on 1982-10-17

ai_review.summary: Excellent audience recording of a high‑energy 1982 Santa Fe Downs show, highlighted by a smoking Throwing Stones/Other One sequence and stellar Brent keyboards.
ai_review.review: Fans rave that this 1982 Santa Fe Downs concert is one of the band’s early‑80s peak performances – an epic first set followed by a second set packed with Throwing Stones, Going Down The Road Feels Bad, Wheel, The Other One, Wharf Rat and Good Lovin', plus standout Althea and Let It Grow.  The audience tape captures the vibe beautifully; it’s crisp and lively despite a few minor glitches (notably a cut in Althea).

ai_rating.rationale: Over twenty detailed, overwhelmingly positive reviews praise both the musical performance and the tape’s sound quality; minor glitches are noted but do not detract from overall enjoyment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑balanced audience recording with occasional glitches (e.g., a brief cut in Althea) but no major dropouts; praised as 'killer' and 'excellent' by multiple reviewers.

standout_songs: Going Down the Road Feels Bad
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as epic; second set even stronger with a long post‑drums stretch that feels like two mini‑shows, seamless transitions and a special Brent verse on Never Trust a Woman.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Strong vocals and 'smoking' guitar tone noted throughout; fans describe it as pure Jerry magic.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as roaring, especially during The Other One, fueling the band’s frenzy.
band_member_comments.Bob: Occasional slide notes mentioned in the jam sections, adding texture.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland praised for a special verse on Never Trust a Woman and overall stellar keyboard work throughout the show.
